name: Button
description: A polymorphic button component supporting multiple variants, sizes, and states including loading. Always renders a <button> element by default, but accepts an `as` prop to render as any element type (e.g., an anchor for link-styled buttons).

notes: When loading, aria-busy is set to true and the button is disabled.
Disabled state uses both the disabled attribute and aria-disabled for maximum compatibility.
Focus indicator uses a 2px outline with a 2px offset using var(--color-border-focus).
When loadingText is provided, it replaces the visible label during loading for screen reader clarity.

variant.description: Visual style of the button. Maps directly to action color tokens.

size.description: Size of the button, controlling padding and font-size.

disabled.description: Disables the button. Applies reduced opacity and prevents interaction.

loading.description: Shows a loading spinner and disables the button. Sets aria-busy=true.

loadingText.description: Optional text to display while loading. Replaces children visually and for screen readers.

leftIcon.description: Icon rendered to the inline-start of the label.

rightIcon.description: Icon rendered to the inline-end of the label.

fullWidth.description: When true, the button stretches to fill its container width.

as.description: The HTML element or React component to render. Use 'a' for link-styled buttons.

type.description: The HTML button type attribute. Defaults to 'button' to avoid accidental form submissions.

className.description: Additional CSS class names to apply.

variants.primary: High-emphasis action. Use for the single most important action on a page or in a section.
variants.secondary: Medium-emphasis action. Use for secondary or alternative actions.
variants.ghost: Low-emphasis action. Use for tertiary actions that should not compete visually.
variants.destructive: Destructive action. Use for delete, remove, or irreversible operations. Always confirm intent before triggering.
variants.link: Inline-style action. Looks like a text link but behaves as a button.

do: Use a single primary button per section or dialog.
Provide loadingText when the loading state needs a descriptive label.
Use the `as` prop with an anchor element when navigating, so keyboard and screen reader behaviour is correct.
Pair leftIcon or rightIcon with concise label text.
dont: Do not use more than one primary button in the same visual group.
Do not disable a button without explaining why (use a tooltip or adjacent helper text).
Do not use the link variant for navigation outside the current context — use a real anchor.
Do not nest interactive elements inside a button.
